problem.text: For real numbers $a$, $b$, and $c$, the roots of the polynomial $$x^5 - 10x^4 + ax^3 + bx^2 + cx - 320$$ form an arithmetic progression. Find $a + b + c$.

steps.title: Where to start: center the progression
steps.body: We know only two coefficients, $-10$ and $-320$, and Vieta's formulas turn those into the sum and the product of the roots. Five roots in arithmetic progression are easiest to handle when written around the middle one: call the middle root $m$ and the common difference $d$, so the roots are $m - 2d$, $m - d$, $m$, $m + d$, $m + 2d$. Then the $d$'s cancel in the sum. Vieta's formulas say the sum of the roots is $10$ (the negative of the $x^4$ coefficient).

your_turn.prompt: Add the five roots and find $m$.

steps.title: Use the product of the roots
steps.body:
For a monic polynomial of degree $5$, the product of the roots is the negative of the constant term, so it is $320$. Pairing $m - d$ with $m + d$ and $m - 2d$ with $m + 2d$:
$$2(4 - d^2)(4 - 4d^2) = 320, \quad\text{so}\quad (4 - d^2)(1 - d^2) = 40$$

steps.title: Find the roots and link them to $a + b + c$
steps.body: An arithmetic progression is understood here to be a list of real numbers, so $d$ is real and we reject $d^2 = -4$. (That value would give the nonreal roots $2 \pm 2i$, $2 \pm 4i$, which the problem's 'arithmetic progression' is meant to exclude.) So $d^2 = 9$, $d = \pm 3$ (the sign only reverses the order), and the roots are $-4, -1, 2, 5, 8$. The polynomial is therefore $(x + 4)(x + 1)(x - 2)(x - 5)(x - 8)$. To reach $a + b + c$ without expanding, plug in $x = 1$, which adds up all the coefficients.

your_turn.prompt: Write the value of $x^5 - 10x^4 + ax^3 + bx^2 + cx - 320$ at $x = 1$ in terms of $a + b + c$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: From the factored form, the value at $x = 1$ is $(5)(2)(-1)(-4)(-7) = -280$. So $a + b + c - 329 = -280$, which gives $a + b + c = 49$. The answer is **$49$**.
